Miguel: Heads-up — ran an apples-to-apples compare between model-v2-quant and model-v2-fp16 using the replay harness (exact prompts + decoding params). Observed a ~20% p99 tail latency regression on quant when the runtime picked the `fused-kv` kernel. The median is fine, tail is where it blows up.

Olivia: Oof. Can you paste the run command + params? Also was this synth traffic or the replay harness?

Miguel: Replay harness. Repro command below:

```
./harness/replay_run.sh --trace-id=20260301-qa --model=model-v2 --variant=quant --decode="temperature=0.0,top_p=0.9,stop=[\"\n\"]" --batch=dynamic --kv-cache=on --tokenizer-align=true
```

Miguel: Key: same prompts, same decode params, same tokenizer seed. Only difference was model artifact (quant vs fp16) and the runtime kernel selection.

Sam: Did you capture a profile (nvprof/perf) around the tail? My gut says KV cache thrash when fused-kv switches in/out during long prefixes. That causes occasional big kernel launches.

Miguel: Yes attached a short perf snippet (pasted):

```
[PROFILE] timeline: 0-300ms kernel_setup, 300-430ms fused_kv_launch, 431-900ms idle/wait, 901-950ms fallback_kernel
[COUNTERS] l2_util spike @ fused_kv_launch, small tensor copies 3x per request
```

Tara: Interesting. Did you warm the KV cache? Replay vs synth can differ: synth often hits ideal batching/warm paths; replay exposes real prefix diversity.

Miguel: I tried warmup=50 requests. Still saw tail spikes on mixed sequence lengths. Synth run (paired with same RNG seed) didn't show the regression.

Olivia: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel selection heuristic uses a seq-length distribution estimate that is biased by the synth harness and picks fused-kv for quant incorrectly; 2) batching heuristic groups heterogeneous sequences causing frequent kernel hot-swaps.

Sam: Agreed. Also check tokenizer alignment: if stop sequences are applied differently between harness and runtime, we might see extra tokens and longer effective sequences. That stresses fused-kv more.

Miguel: Tokenizer check: we used `--tokenizer-align=true` but I'll re-run with a forced exact tokenization replay: `--tokenizer-seedfile=exact_tokens.json`.

deploy-bot: Deployed runtime change 2026-02-28T14:03:19Z — kernel_selection: adaptive_fused_preference=true (cherry-picked #4217).

Miguel: Aha — that deploy lines up with when we first saw increased field p99 in customer telemetry. Could be related.

Tara: For an apples-to-apples controlled experiment we should:
- freeze kernel selection (force baseline kernel)
- run replay harness with exact token sequences (no tokenizer on-the-fly)
- run synth harness with identical token sequences and same decode params
- collect nvprof + tracing + per-request kernel selection logs

Olivia: Also include a run with `--batch=strict:1` (single-request batches) to see if the batching heuristic is amplifying the effect. If single-batch removes the tail, it's batching-related.

Sam: Quick config snippet to force baseline kernel:

```
runtime.config.override = {
  kernel_selection: {
    mode: "force",
    kernel: "baseline-kv"
  }
}
```

Miguel: I'll kick off these four runs now (quant/fp16 x forced/default kernel x strict/dynamic batch) and attach results. ETA ~45m.

perf-bot: Started job 1768204820-1 (quant, replay, forced-baseline, strict-batch). Logs: https://internal.perf/redwood/job/1768204820-1

Miguel: First quick observation (prelim): forcing baseline kernel removes the p99 spike for quant in strict-batch. Dynamic-batch + forced-baseline still shows a few spikes but much reduced.

Olivia: That points to an interaction: kernel selection + batching heuristics. If the adaptive fused preference is toggling kernels mid-stream when batch composition changes, we get kernel churn.

Sam: We should capture kernel-selection decision points in trace logs and correlate with batch composition. Add a short trace hook that logs: `batch_id, chosen_kernel, seq_lengths, kv_cache_state` per request.

Miguel: Will add that hook and re-run the dynamic-batch case. Also re-run the synth harness but feed it the exact token sequences from the replay to rule out tokenizer differences.

Tara: For postmortem: if confirmed, rollback deploy flag `adaptive_fused_preference` and add a safe mode that prevents kernel switching during active requests (only on allocation boundaries).

Miguel: Also filing a test case in the harness repo: `tests/regression/kernel-batch-kv-switching.py` that simulates mixed prefix lengths and asserts no kernel hot-switch during active sequence processing.

Olivia: Great. Please paste the job links when done. We'll triage with infra and runtime owners. :thumbsup:

Miguel: Will do. Thanks all.
